content: Ascorbic acid, commonly known as vitamin C, is prescribed to prevent and treat scurvy, a condition caused by a deficiency of vitamin C in the body. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Ascorbic acid is available in various forms, including extended-release capsules and tablets, lozenges, syrup, chewable tablets, and liquid drops, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken once daily. Follow the instructions on the packaging or your prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist for clarification. Take ascorbic acid exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed. Some tablets are meant to be chewed, while others should be swallowed whole with a full glass of water. It may take up to three weeks for symptoms of scurvy to improve. Before taking ascorbic acid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ascorbic acid or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including other vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney stones. If you have diabetes, consult your doctor or pharmacist about the correct method for testing your urine while taking large amounts of ascorbic acid. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ascorbic acid, contact your doctor immediately. Certain forms of ascorbic acid contain sodium and should be avoided if you are on a sodiumor salt-restricted diet. Your doctor may recommend dietary changes to increase your vitamin C intake. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ascorbic acid may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent diarrhea or an upset stomach. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
